name: AI GuardWall – AI-Powered Digital Security Guardian
author: SoftVoltAI

sections.description:
AI GuardWall watches your WordPress site the way a good security engineer would. It scans every file and database record for malware, lets an AI analyst read each suspicious finding and explain it, blocks attacks at the firewall, hardens the installation step by step, and gives you the admin tools that WordPress itself lacks.

Malware scanner

  • WordPress core and repository plugins are verified file by file against WordPress.org checksums: modified, unknown and missing files are reported.
  • Everything that cannot be verified (plugins, themes, MU plugins, drop-ins, uploads, wp-config.php, .htaccess, JavaScript, CSS, images and text files) is read for web shells, backdoors, encoded payload loaders, hidden admin creation, obfuscation, SEO spam, hidden links and iframes, redirect malware, miners, card skimmers and known malware families.
  • The database is inspected too: posts, post meta, options (widgets, theme code boxes), comments, users (rogue and hidden administrators), roles (privilege escalation), cron jobs and unknown tables.
  • Configuration checks: outdated software, debug output, weak salts, file permissions, HTTPS, exposed readme and debug log, REST user listing, directory listing.
  • Known vulnerabilities in WordPress, plugins and themes (WPVulnerability database, when you switch it on), plugins closed on WordPress.org or abandoned for two years.
  • Backups, database dumps, .env, .git and phpinfo files that can be downloaded, full path disclosure, a browsable uploads folder, administrator passwords that are among the most common ones, the server on spam block lists and Google Safe Browsing (when you switch them on), the SSL certificate and free disk space.
  • Your own signatures (text or regular expressions) and wildcard exclusions.
  • File-change monitoring between scans, with the updates you installed recognised.
  • Runs in steps, so hosts with short PHP limits finish; scheduled twice a day, daily, every other day, on weekdays, at weekends or weekly.

AI malware analyst

When you ask for it, an AI model reads a finding with the bundled malware detection & cleanup instructions and answers with a verdict (confirmed malware, suspicious, likely legitimate, needs manual review), its confidence, why, what could break and the safest fix. It sends nothing until you agree to what is sent (see External services); passwords, keys and email addresses are removed first.

Works with free models (OpenRouter, Groq, Google Gemini), any OpenAI-compatible service, your own paid key for Claude, GPT and DeepSeek, or your Claude Pro or Max plan through Claude Desktop (MCP), with no API key. Import your own .md knowledge files to teach the analyst your rules.

Cleanup, safely

Every finding comes with a How to fix it guide: which button to press, what to do by hand when no button can, and where to go. The cleanup plan groups the open findings in the order a cleanup is done (remove confirmed malware, re-install modified files, clean the database, check accounts and tasks, review what is unsure, close the doors) and runs each step on every finding at once. Quarantine, delete (a sealed copy is kept for 30 days), remove injected code from posts and options, trash records, remove cron jobs, delete rogue users. A Markdown report lists every finding with file, line, severity, confidence, verdict, why, recommendation and how to fix it.

Database cleanup

The Database page cleans revisions, spam, transients and orphaned data, optimizes the tables and removes the ones nothing installed uses, on demand or on a schedule, with a backup of the touched tables first.

Firewall

  • Rule sets for SQL injection, XSS, file inclusion, code execution, malicious uploads, scanner tools, sensitive paths and XML-RPC amplification; repeat attackers are locked out; a learning mode that switches to blocking on a date you choose.
  • Rate limits for people, crawlers and 404 scanners, with verified Google and Bing crawlers never limited.
  • Threat intelligence (when you switch it on): the Spamhaus DROP lists of criminal networks, updated daily, plus your own block lists.
  • Advanced blocking: user agents, referrers, host names, unusual HTTP methods, blank POST requests, honeypot URLs that lock the visitor out, fake Googlebots.
  • The 6G rules in .htaccess, rolled back automatically if the server answers 500. A message of your own on the block page, and an unlock link by email for locked-out administrators.

Login security

  • Login attempt limits with escalating lockouts, limits on password reset requests, hidden error details, honeypot, instant lockout for attack usernames, strong-password rules, breached-password check, idle logout.
  • Two-factor authentication (authenticator apps and emailed codes) with backup codes, per-role enforcement and a grace period; XML-RPC logins refused for accounts that use 2FA.
  • Passkeys: sign in with a fingerprint, face, phone or security key (WebAuthn, on HTTPS sites). A passkey counts as the second factor.
  • Hidden login URL, a login door that opens only with your secret word, and an extra HTTP password before wp-admin or the whole site.

Spam, forms and users

  • CAPTCHA on login, registration, lost password, comments and WooCommerce forms: the built-in maths question, Cloudflare Turnstile or Google reCAPTCHA v2/v3.
  • Comment spam: honeypot and time check, spam sent to the spam folder or thrown away, old spam emptied, repeat spammers locked out, the addresses with the most spam listed with a Block button.
  • Registrations: honeypot, reserved names, approval by hand.
  • Who is logged in right now and from where, with forced logout; a maximum session length; administrators and editors with their last login, 2FA and passkeys; display names that show the login name fixed in one click.

Live traffic

Visits, logins, failed logins, pages not found and every blocked request as they happen, with filters, the busiest addresses of the day, and Block and WHOIS buttons on every line.

Hardening wizard

Every protection, grouped like the WordPress security guide, each with what it does and what could break. Tick what you want, or start from the Basic, Recommended or Maximum preset. .htaccess rules are rolled back automatically when the server answers 500.

Security Wall tools

Change the admin email without the confirmation mail, rename any user (get rid of “admin”), rotate the security keys and salts (by hand or on a schedule), check and fix file permissions, change the database table prefix (with a full backup first), look up who owns an IP address or domain, test the connections the plugin needs and the email, read the PHP error log, and an emergency switch that turns every protection off. Settings can be exported, imported on another site, or reset.

Site tools

Tools that usually need a plugin each, switched on one by one on the Tools page and adding nothing to the site while off: disable comments, maintenance or coming-soon mode, reCAPTCHA v3 (also for WooCommerce, Contact Form 7, WPForms and Elementor Pro forms), custom post types and taxonomies, duplicate posts, drag-and-drop ordering, redirects with a 404 log, custom permalinks and a broken link checker.

Admin tools

A user role editor (nobody can lock themselves out), switch to user (logged, never to administrators), every scheduled task with Run and Delete, email through SMTP with a test and an optional log, and admin area settings for the admin bar, dashboard boxes and update notices.

Alerts

Email for scan results, new administrators, logins, lockouts, attack surges, breached passwords, vulnerable software, the firewall switched off, and a site monitor that checks every 15 minutes whether the site answers and how fast, with a daily or weekly summary.

Credits

The QR code on the two-factor setup screen is drawn in the browser by the bundled jquery-qrcode library (QRCode for JavaScript by Kazuhiko Arase, MIT license). Nothing is loaded from elsewhere for it.

External services

AI GuardWall connects to the services below, each only for the feature named and only with the data listed. Requests the plugin labels itself carry the user agent “AI-GuardWall/”; the others carry WordPress’s standard user agent, which includes your site’s address.

The AI provider you choose

Nothing is sent until you connect a provider on Malware Cleanup > 1. AI model, tick “I agree” in step 2 (“Allow and save”) there, and press an AI button yourself (analyse one finding, the selected ones or all open ones). The request goes to the provider you picked, with your own API key, and contains: the suspicious code (the lines around each match, or the whole file when it is small), the file path or the database table and row (post, option, user name or cron hook) with the suspicious content, the scanner’s reasons, your site’s host name, the WordPress and PHP versions, the active theme, the name of the plugin or theme the file belongs to, and the cleanup instructions and knowledge files you switched on.

Never sent: before anything leaves your site, the database login, the security keys and salts, passwords and password hashes, API keys and tokens, private keys and email addresses are removed from it. From files that hold credentials by nature (wp-config.php, .env, SQL dumps, key files) only the matched lines are sent, never the whole file. Visitor data from the firewall and the activity log is never sent. “Test connection” sends one fixed test message and nothing about your site.

  • OpenRouter: terms, privacy. “Show every free model” also asks OpenRouter for its public model list; nothing about your site is sent.
  • Groq: terms, privacy
  • Google Gemini API: terms, privacy
  • Anthropic (Claude): terms, privacy
  • OpenAI: terms, privacy
  • DeepSeek: terms, privacy
  • Any OpenAI-compatible service you enter yourself, under that service’s own terms.

Claude Desktop (MCP), if you choose it

Only if you choose Anthropic > Claude Desktop (MCP) on the AI model page, agree in step 2 and set Claude Desktop up. Your server then sends nothing to Anthropic. Claude Desktop, on your own computer, signs in to your site with an application password you create and, through the MCP Adapter plugin, uses the tools AI GuardWall adds: a summary of the latest scan, the open findings with the same text the analyst would send to a provider (the code around each match, with the secrets listed above removed), and a tool that saves its verdicts. It never deletes, cleans or changes a file. What the tools return goes from Claude Desktop to Anthropic under your Claude plan’s terms: consumer terms, privacy. Revoke the application password to disconnect it.

WordPress.org

Scans compare WordPress core and plugins from WordPress.org with the official checksums (api.wordpress.org, downloads.wordpress.org) and ask api.wordpress.org whether installed plugins were closed or abandoned. Sent: the WordPress version and language, and the slugs and versions of the installed plugins. New security keys are made on your own site; nothing is fetched for them. WordPress.org privacy

WPVulnerability

Off until you tick the WPVulnerability check under Malware Cleanup > Scan settings > Extra checks. Then each scan asks the WPVulnerability database (www.wpvulnerability.net) whether the installed WordPress version, plugins and themes have known vulnerabilities. Sent: their slugs and version numbers. Terms, privacy

Spamhaus and other block lists

Off until you switch on “Block known malicious networks” (Security Wall > Firewall, or the Recommended preset). Then the plugin downloads the Spamhaus DROP lists from www.spamhaus.org once a day; nothing about your site is sent. Terms, privacy

Off until you tick the block list check under Malware Cleanup > Scan settings > Extra checks. Then each scan looks up your server’s IP address in three DNS block lists: zen.spamhaus.org (Spamhaus, links above), bl.spamcop.net (SpamCop, Cisco privacy) and b.barracudacentral.org (Barracuda Reputation Block List, privacy).

Pwned Passwords (Have I Been Pwned)

The Pwned Passwords service of Have I Been Pwned (api.pwnedpasswords.com) tells whether a password appeared in a data breach. It is used only when “Block passwords found in data breaches” is on (off by default): when an administrator logs in or chooses a password, the first 5 characters of the password’s SHA-1 hash are sent (k-anonymity range search) and the matching hash suffixes come back; the password itself and the rest of the hash never leave your server. Terms of use, privacy policy

Google Safe Browsing

Only when you enter your own Safe Browsing API key in the scan settings: the scan sends your site’s address to Google to see whether it is listed as unsafe. Terms, privacy

Cloudflare Turnstile and Google reCAPTCHA

Only when you choose one of them as the CAPTCHA (Security Wall > Brute force), or switch on the reCAPTCHA v3 site tool for Contact Form 7, WPForms or Elementor forms: the protected forms load the provider’s script from challenges.cloudflare.com or www.google.com, and when a form is sent, the visitor’s answer token and IP address go to the provider to be checked. “Test the keys” on the reCAPTCHA card loads the script in the admin and sends one test token. Turnstile: terms, privacy. reCAPTCHA: terms, privacy

rdap.org (WHOIS)

When you press WHOIS next to an IP address or a domain, that address or domain is sent to rdap.org, which passes the question to the registry responsible for it. About and fair use

Links in your content

Only when the broken link checker is switched on (Tools > Site features): the links in your posts and pages are requested once a day to see whether they still work. Nothing else is sent.

Your mail server (SMTP)

Only when you switch on SMTP in Tools > Admin tools > Email: WordPress emails are sent through the mail server you enter, signing in with the login you give. Nothing else is sent to it.

Connection test

Only when you press “Test the connections” on Security Wall > Tools: each of the services above is requested once, without any data about your site, to show whether your server can reach it.

Checks of your own site (the site monitor, exposed-file probes, the .htaccess safety test) only request your own address.

Your visitors

The firewall, the login protection and the activity log keep their records (IP address, browser, requested address, time) in your own database, to block attacks and show you what happened. Passwords, password-reset keys, nonces and tokens in addresses are not recorded. Nothing of it is sent to SoftVoltAI or anyone else, and the plugin does not track anyone. To tell real Google and Bing crawlers from fakes, the firewall looks up a visitor’s IP address in DNS (reverse lookup) through your server’s own resolver; the result is cached for a day. The plugin adds a suggested text for your privacy policy (Settings > Privacy).
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install it from Plugins > Add New.
  2. Activate it. The firewall, login protection and the safe hardening defaults are on at once.
  3. Connect an AI model on AI GuardWall > Malware Cleanup > 1. AI model (a free one is fine to start).
  4. Run the first scan from Malware Cleanup > 3. Scan.
  5. Walk through Security Wall > Dashboard.
sections.faq:
Does the AI see my site?

Only after you agree to it on the AI model page, and only when you ask for an analysis: then the suspicious code (the lines around each match, or a small file whole), the file path or database row, the scanner’s reasons and basic site facts go to the AI provider you chose. Database logins, keys, salts, passwords, tokens and email addresses are removed first, files such as wp-config.php are never sent whole, and visitor data is never sent. With Claude Desktop (MCP) your server sends nothing to an AI provider: Claude Desktop on your computer reads the same findings through the tools AI GuardWall adds, and only after you agreed.

Can it break my site?

The plugin never deletes anything outright: a copy of every file it removes is kept in its database for 30 days, and database content is backed up before it is cleaned. .htaccess rules are removed again if the server answers 500. Rules marked “Check after enabling” tell you what to test.

I am locked out. What now?

Add define( 'SVABG_SAFE_MODE', true ); to wp-config.php (by FTP or your host’s file manager). Every protection is off while the line is there; log in, fix the setting, and remove the line again. When you can still log in, Security Wall > Tools > Emergency switch does the same with one click and turns everything back on with another.

What does Pro add?

AI GuardWall Pro is a separate plugin that works on top of this one: keep AI GuardWall – AI-Powered Digital Security Guardian active and add Pro next to it, and your settings stay. It adds automatic AI analysis after scheduled scans, an AI-written site report and hardening advice, country blocking, CSV/JSON exports, and hands-on tools: a File Manager, a Database Manager, code snippets and your own .htaccess rules. Nothing in this plugin is locked or limited, and it needs no account or license key.
sections.changelog:
1.5.4

  • New: Claude Desktop (MCP) as the AI analyst, with your Claude Pro or Max plan and no API key. Press Analyse and the request waits for Claude; in Claude Desktop you ask it to answer, and the page picks up the verdicts by itself. Needs WordPress 6.9 or later, the MCP Adapter plugin and an application password.
  • A site has one Claude Desktop connection, shared by every plugin that works with Claude Desktop: when it is connected through another plugin, AI GuardWall shows it as connected too, and its config entry is named after your site.
  • AI model page: the same layout as SoftVoltAI’s other plugins. A summary of the connection, the open findings the AI has read and where the AI works, then the providers in tabs (Free to start, Paid, Other ways) with Claude Desktop as a way to connect Anthropic, then 2. Allow and save and 3. How much to think.
  • Scanner: a method with the same name as a shell function (for example $pdo->exec() or Prompt::system()) is no longer reported as “Shell/system function usage”. Real calls of system(), exec() and the others are still reported.

1.5.3

  • First release on WordPress.org.
